roles.name: Capital Program Analyst
roles.blurb: Plans, funds, tracks and reports the capital program across thousands of projects, and supports rate cases with the evidence behind them.

areas.name: Capital plan (CIP)
areas.what: Builds and keeps the 5-year capital improvement plan from master plans, asset needs, mandates and growth.
tasks: Collect project requests from engineering and operations
Maintain the 5-year CIP and its annual update
Calendarize spend by month (Jan Calendarization)
Tie projects to mandates (lead service lines, PFAS treatment)
Track what changed between plan vintages

areas.name: Prioritization and business cases
areas.what: Ranks projects by risk and value and makes the case for the funded list.
tasks: Score projects on asset risk, compliance and customer value
Recommend the funded list within each utility envelope
Prepare business cases for the WIN gate
Record the alternatives considered

areas.name: Budgeting and funding
areas.what: Turns the plan into approved budgets and lines up the money to pay for them.
tasks: Prepare the annual capital budget per utility
Process WIN authorizations and budget transfers
Track funding sources (SRF loans, WIFIA, PFAS grants, contributions)
Forecast capital cash flow for Treasury

areas.name: Cost tracking and forecasting
areas.what: Keeps actuals, commitments and forecasts current for every project and explains the variances.
tasks: Report monthly actuals against plan and forecast
Track commitments, open orders and retainage
Keep the forecast at completion current with project managers
Explain variances above threshold
Track change orders and contingency use
Check the program can spend the annual plan by December

areas.name: Schedule and delivery
areas.what: Follows milestones and critical paths and what slippage does to spend.
tasks: Track milestones against the baseline schedule
Flag critical path slippage and its effect on spend
Follow stage gates from planning to close-out

areas.name: Rate case and regulatory support
areas.what: Provides the capital schedules, eligible plant and evidence the four commissions ask for.
tasks: Prepare capital schedules and rate base additions for rate cases
Answer data requests from commission staff and intervenors
Support DSIC and SIC surcharge filings with eligible plant
Confirm in-service dates for projects claimed in a test year
Keep the prudence record (decisions, alternatives, approvals)

areas.name: Capital accounting and close-out
areas.what: Keeps CWIP, AFUDC and plant in service right and closes finished projects.
tasks: Apply the capitalization policy (capital or expense)
Review CWIP balances and AFUDC
Move completed projects to plant in service
Close out finished projects and release unused budget
Record retirements of replaced assets

areas.name: Grant and loan compliance
areas.what: Keeps SRF, WIFIA and PFAS grant work compliant and draws the money on time.
tasks: Prepare SRF and WIFIA draw requests
Track Davis-Bacon and Build America, Buy America records
Report lead service line replacement progress
Report to lenders and funding agencies

areas.name: Program reporting
areas.what: Tells the Capital Steering Committee, leadership and the commissions where the program stands.
tasks: Write the monthly capital program report
Prepare the quarterly Capital Steering Committee review
Answer ad hoc questions from leadership
Keep the program dashboard current

questions.q: What changed between the 2026 and 2027 capital plans, and why?

answer.text: The 2027-2031 plan is $6.42B, up $214M on the 2026 vintage. Most of the increase is the Federal PFAS Program in Belmara and Ardenia (+$151M) and the lead service line program brought forward in Ardenia (+$88M). Thirty-one renewal projects moved out to 2031 or later (-$25M).

questions.q: How much of the 5-year plan is driven by mandates rather than discretionary renewal?

answer.text: $3.04B of the $6.42B plan is tied to a government mandate: PFAS treatment, lead service line replacement and two consent orders in Dunmoor. Another $0.58B is committed to third parties.

questions.q: Which unfunded projects carry the highest risk, and what would funding the top five cost?

answer.text: Five unfunded priority 1 projects carry Intolerable asset risk, led by the Kestrel Valley clearwell replacement. Funding all five would cost $38.6M over 2027-2029. The ranking uses the project-level risk rating in the PMO master; there is no asset-level condition score connected.
sources: pmo.project · Asset Risk Assessment, CAPEX Priority Level

questions.q: How much of next year’s capital spend is covered by SRF loans and grants?

answer.figLabel: of 2027 forecast spend has a loan or grant
answer.text: $226M of the $1.23B forecast for 2027 is covered by executed SRF loan agreements and two PFAS grants. Another $41M has applications pending, including the $18.5M Belmara SRF loan for Quarrydown WTP.
sources: Funding tracker: SRF, WIFIA, PFAS grants

questions.q: Which large projects in delivery are forecast to overrun their approved budget by more than 10%?

answer.text: Nine of 1,419 large projects in delivery are more than 10% over their approved budget, $6.21M together. Six have a WIN budget revision in the Level 03 queue; three have none: the Kestrel Valley clearwell, Jarrowfield WTP and the Bellwater PFAS install. Dunmoor East Filter Media Renewal is still on its June figure (+6.1%) and its manager expects it above 10% when the Lakeshore batch lands on 23 October.

questions.q: Why is Dunmoor East Filter Media Renewal over budget?

answer.text: On Dunmoor East, change orders have used the whole contingency and $0.43M more: concrete deterioration in the filter walls (CO-001, $1.88M), asbestos gasket abatement (CO-002, $0.64M), the engineer’s floor investigation ($0.40M), a media credit (−$0.41M), filter floors out of level in Filters 8, 9 and 11 (CO-003, $1.21M) and a 214-day extension (CO-004, $0.85M). The rest of the $5.5M is the extension’s owner costs, interest, escalation and a $2.1M risk on Filters 10 and 12.
sources: Contracts and change orders: DEF-2023-C01, DEF-2026-C02, Exhibit F logs
Mail thread "Dunmoor East filters: Phase 2 floors"

questions.q: How much contingency is left across the program, and where is it going?

answer.text: $92M of $224M contingency remains. 58% of the draw went to treatment plant projects (PFAS and filters); network blankets have used 19% of theirs.

questions.q: Are we on track to spend the FY26 plan by December?

answer.figLabel: of the FY26 plan by December
answer.text: Posted actuals to 30 September are $812.0M against $844.5M planned, and the working forecast for October to December is $297.8M: $1,109.8M against the $1,180.0M plan, so $70.2M would move into FY27. The gap sits in PFAS projects in Belmara and the Lakeshore projects that have not been re-forecast since June.

questions.q: Which large projects slipped on their critical path this month?
What does schedule slippage on large projects do to this year’s spend?
How does plant placed in service compare with what the last Belmara rate order assumed?

answer.figLabel: of plant additions the order assumed
answer.text: Through Q3 2026, $247M has been placed in service in Belmara against $264M assumed in the 2025 BPUC order for the same period. The order allows $431M over 2025-2027.
sources: Rate cases and orders: BPUC 2025 order, Appendix C

questions.q: Which projects claimed in the Belmara test year are now at risk of missing it?

answer.text: Seven of the 38 projects claimed in service by 31 December 2026 now carry an in-service date in 2027, $41.3M of rate base. Two of the 38 have no row in the in-service file, so they are checked from the forecast phase only.
sources: Rate cases and orders: BPUC test-year schedule

questions.q: What evidence do we have that the Dunmoor East cost increase was prudent?

answer.text: The record holds the condition finding (structural investigation, Amendment No. 2), the engineer’s two priced alternatives for the filter floors, the WIN Level 03 approval of CO-003 and the committee note of 6 August. No record shows that rebidding the Phase 2 work was considered.
sources: Contracts and change orders: DEF-2026-C02 CO-003 file

questions.q: Which projects are in service but still sitting in CWIP?

answer.text: 46 projects with an in-service date before 1 August still carry an open CWIP balance of $31.8M; 12 of them are in Dunmoor, where unitization is three months behind.

questions.q: How much AFUDC have we accrued this year, by project?

answer.text: $24.7M year to date. The PFAS projects at Quarrydown and Yarnton account for $6.9M of it.

questions.q: Which SRF-funded contracts are missing Build America, Buy America records?

answer.text: Three of 22 SRF-funded contracts have no current BABA certification: the Quarrydown vessel supply (Ridgeform), the Westbrook restoration term agreement and one Selby Point valve order.
sources: Funding tracker: SRF, WIFIA, PFAS grants
Contracts and change orders: certification folders

questions.q: How many lead service lines have we replaced this year against plan?
Give me a one-page summary of the capital program for the Capital Steering Committee.

answer.text: Drafted from the overrun, plan delivery, rate order and freshness results: $812M posted of a $1.18B FY26 plan (94% expected by December), nine large projects above 10% with Dunmoor East expected to cross on 23 October, Belmara plant additions at 94% of the order. Schedule items are left out because Primavera P6 is not connected.
sources: Results of the questions on overruns, plan delivery and plant additions

questions.q: Which projects have not been re-forecast for more than 45 days?

answer.text: 63 large projects in the Lakeshore Region have no working forecast since the 6+6 round of 15 June, after the Lakeshore project office moved to a new project controls tool. They hold $612.4M of approved budget. All 63 re-forecasts load in one catch-up batch on Friday 23 October.
sources: Mail thread "Lakeshore forecasts: 63 projects still on June figures"
